| [NOTE-1096](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1096.md) | Flayelle et al. — A taxonomy of technology design features that promote potentially addictive online behaviours | A narrative review and a taxonomy. Design features of six kinds of online service are linked, mostly by cross-sectional, qualitative or indirect evidence, to loss of control. They are sorted by the learning and control process each exploits. Model-free: reinforcement schedules and personalized triggers. Model-based: overvaluation, interference with deliberation, partial goal fulfilment, cognitive biases. Providers select features by their effect on use and revenue, and personalize them under informational asymmetry. For the record it maps closely onto the parts of the potential account: features that strengthen a cue-keyed ranking, move its reference course, falsify the user's reading of progress, or pre-empt the other perspectives. | Read |
| [NOTE-1101](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1101.md) | The current status of research on the structure of evaluative space | The evaluative space model restated by its authors. Positivity and negativity are separable systems whose combined output is a bipolar approach–avoid predisposition. They can be activated reciprocally, independently or together. Coactivation is ambivalence, which is rare, arousing and behaviourally indeterminate, and gives the same net output as neutrality. Negativity has the higher gain and positivity the higher intercept, and both recalibrate with context. Evaluation is heterarchical, with higher levels able to override lower. | Read |
| [NOTE-1102](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1102.md) | Control Theory, Goal Attainment, and Psychopathology | A commentary. Control theory adds to goal talk the need to perceive the present state and compare it with the goal. Psychopathology arises where the loop's input, reference value, comparison or output is extreme or biased. The five factors are sensitivities to classes of goals. Valence tracks the velocity of goal attainment against a reference value, so approach and avoidance can each produce either sign. Confidence, doubt and disengagement lie outside the loop, in expectancy-value theory. | Read |
| [NOTE-1109](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1109.md) | Berridge and Robinson — Liking, wanting, and the incentive-sensitization theory of addiction | An invited review of the incentive-sensitization theory by its authors. | [NOTE-1250](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1250.md) | Trauma, prejudice, large-group identity and psychoanalysis | A memorial lecture at the Freud Museum. Large-group identity is a tent's canvas worn over each person's individual identity, fixed in childhood through what parents deposit and unchangeable after adolescence. In two decades of unofficial dialogues, Volkan saw participants who felt their large-group identity threatened turn, with emotion, to an injury their ancestors suffered centuries ago. The shared image of such an event, real or mythologized, changes function across generations and becomes an identity marker: a chosen trauma. It feeds entitlement to recover what was lost and, in a "time collapse", makes the old event feel recent, as with Kosovo 1389 under Milošević. The Holocaust is not a chosen trauma: it is recent, its stories are alive, and it is mourned rather than kept as a wound for revenge. | Read |
